title: Working at Redwood — Hiring, Onboarding, Roles, Benefits, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Mitchell
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page is the canonical company handbook reference for new and existing Redwood employees. It consolidates our working principles, role and career ladder summaries, hiring and onboarding process, benefits and perks, and a practical guide to core internal tools. This doc is maintained by People Ops; see the Ownership section for contacts and SLAs.

Quick links: People Ops home, Engineering handbook, IT & Security, Payroll & Benefits portal.

1) Working at Redwood — high level

- Our culture values: shipping, clarity, ownership, and empathy. We balance rapid iteration with production reliability.
- Operating hours: core collaboration hours are 10:00–16:00 PT. Flexible schedules are supported with manager approval.
- Remote-first: Redwood supports remote work with region-aware policies (see Remote Work policy). Onsite expectations for incubator teams will be communicated by managers.

2) Roles and career ladders (summary)

- Purpose: Provide a clear, consistent framework for expectations, leveling conversations, and promotion cycles.
- Scope: Engineering, Product, Design, SRE, Applied ML, DevRel, Sales, Customer Success, People Ops, Finance.

Representative ladder summary (short):

| Function | IC progression | Typical years | Core expectations |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Engineering | IC2 -> IC3 -> IC4 -> IC5 -> IC6 | 1–3 -> 2–4 -> 3–5 -> 4+ -> 7+ | Contribute to product features -> Lead project ownership -> Architect and mentor -> Org-level impact -> Strategic technical leader |
| Product | PM1 -> PM2 -> PM3 -> PM4 | 1–3 -> 2–4 -> 3–6 -> 5+ | Feature discovery -> Cross-team execution -> Product strategy -> Portfolio leadership |

- Promotion cadence: formal calibration and promotion windows twice per year (May, November). Managers should open promotion conversations at least 8 weeks prior to calibration.
- Evidence used in promotions: impact statements, peer feedback, manager assessment, project artifacts, metrics (SLIs, adoption), and customer feedback where relevant.

3) Hiring process (standardized workflow)

Objective: Consistent candidate experience and high signal for role fit. People Ops and Hiring Managers are responsible for compliance with EEO policies.

High-level steps (candidate-facing):
1. Requisition approval (hiring manager creates req in Greenhouse; compensation band approved by People Ops).
2. Sourcing & screening (recruiter screens, 30-minute intro call).
3. Technical / role interviews (interview loop scheduled; use standardized rubrics stored in Interview Kits).
4. Take-home / assignment (optional; should be timeboxed to <= 4 hours).
5. Final interview + hiring manager debrief.
6. Offer & negotiation (People Ops drafts offer; hiring manager approves final comp).
7. Background check & reference checks.
8. Onboarding start date coordination and preboarding.

Interview loop guidance (for hiring managers):
- Use the published Interview Kit for the role. Kits include: role spec, rubric, sample questions, and scoring guide.
- Interviewers must submit scores within 48 hours; missing feedback delays the loop.
- Diversity & inclusion: ensure slates include diverse candidates and that interview panels have at least one trained interviewer in unconscious bias.

4) Offer & compensation bands

- Bands are published internally in Compensation Bands (People Ops intranet). For initial budgeting, consult the located bands and target comp within +/- 10% of midpoint depending on market and candidate.
- Approval workflow: Hiring manager -> Recruiting Director -> People Ops compensation -> Finance for headcount > $X (band threshold).

5) Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)

Overview: Onboarding is a structured triplet: Preboarding (before day 1), Week 1 (setup & orientation), 30–90 day ramp (deliverables & 1:1 cadence).

Preboarding (2–14 days before):
- People Ops sends offer packet, benefits link, and first-day schedule.
- IT provisions laptop and account access; new hire receives device tracking link.
- Manager assigns buddy and shares first-week goals.

Day 1 & Week 1:
- Orientation (People Ops): company mission, org chart, policies, security training (basic).
- Team onboarding: product overview, codebase tour, roadmap, and immediate contributor task.
- Accounts & access: ensure access to Slack, GitHub, JIRA, Notion, Redwood Console demo account, and HRIS. See Internal Tools section for links and quick commands.

30–90 day ramp:
- 30-day check-in (manager + new hire).
- 60-day technical/role checkpoint with mentor and engineering lead.
- 90-day review: outcomes assessment and confirmation of leveling band.

Onboarding deliverable examples (for engineers):
- Complete a small bug/feature with code review and CI pass.
- Run the end-to-end local dev environment setup without assistance.
- Document a short runbook for the feature or infra touched.

6) Benefits & perks (high-level)

Core benefits:
- Medical, dental, vision (US plans with premium and high-deductible options).
- 401(k) with company match up to 4% (US).
- Equity: RSU or option grants, cadence documented in Offer Letter.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 6 weeks secondary (global variations handled by People Ops).
- PTO: 20 days vacation + company holidays and discretionary wellness days.
- Parental & caregiver support: fertility & adoption benefits, backup childcare stipend.

Work from home stipend & hardware: one-time remote setup allowance ($1,000) and annual ergonomic budget.
Learning & development: $1,200 annual learning stipend; internal mentorship & technical laddering workshops.
Wellness: mental health EAP, monthly wellness allowance, and quarterly wellbeing sessions.

How to enroll: Use the Benefits portal (link in People Ops home). Enrollment window is 30 days from start date; changes allowed during Open Enrollment (annually in November) or qualifying life event.

7) Internal tools guide — quick start commands and ownership

This section lists the most-used internal systems and the basic steps to get productive. For full step-by-step instructions, follow links to each tool's page.

- Slack (communication)
  - Workspace: redwoodhq.slack.com
  - Core channels: #all, #engineering, #product, #people-ops, #sre-alerts, #random
  - Tip: Use /whois and pinned messages for quick contact lookups.

- GitHub (code)
  - Organization: github.com/redwood-inference
  - Repo permissions: team-based access via GitHub teams. Request access via the GitHub Access request form.
  - Branching: follow trunk-based workflow; create PRs with a linked JIRA ticket.

- JIRA (issues & planning)
  - Project keys: ENG, PLAT, SRE, DOCS, CS
  - Sprint cadence: 2-week sprints for core engineering teams.
  - Templates: use the "Incident" and "Release" issue templates for consistency.

- Notion / Confluence (documentation)
  - Confluence is the authoritative place for service runbooks and process docs. Use the company-handbook and eng-* spaces.
  - Notion is used for playbooks and whiteboards. Ensure Confluence pages link to Notion design docs for version history.

- Redwood Console (internal demo & sandbox)
  - Sandbox URL: console.internal.redwood.ai (VPN or SSO required for Private regions).
  - Demo credentials provisioned by Platform team.
  - Tip: use the API key rotation feature for demo accounts to avoid stale secrets.

- CI/CD & Builds
  - Primary pipeline: CircleCI and self-hosted build runners for GPU images.
  - Release process: create a release branch, run the release pipeline (circleci pipeline trigger --branch release/X.Y) and follow the Release checklist.

Quick CLI snippets (copy/paste in terminal):
- Request GitHub access (example web form): open "https://docs.internal/redwood/git-access"
- Trigger a CircleCI pipeline: curl -X POST -u $CIRCLE_TOKEN: "https://circleci.com/api/v2/project/gh/redwood-inference/service/pipeline?branch=main"
- Fetch onboarding docs: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $HR_TOKEN" "https://hr.internal/redwood/api/onboarding/newhire?email=you@company.com"

8) Security & compliance basics for new hires

- Mandatory trainings: Security Fundamentals and Data Handling training must be completed within the first 14 days.
- Passwords & MFA: Company SSO + enforced MFA (Auth app or hardware key).
- Access requests: follow least-privilege principle; request temporary elevated access through the Access Request form.

9) Manager checklist & responsibilities

Managers must:
- Create a 90-day plan within 3 business days of start.
- Assign a peer buddy and a mentor.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 90 days.
- Provide written feedback for promotion packets and keep calibration deadlines.

10) FAQs & edge cases

Q: Who do I contact for payroll errors?
A: Payroll inbox (payroll@redwood.ai) and People Ops lead (Ava Mitchell).

Q: Can I change my start date?
A: Yes; notify People Ops at least 10 business days prior. People Ops will coordinate comp and benefits windows.

Q: What if I need additional equipment?
A: Submit a Hardware Request ticket (IT portal). Standard laptop refresh cadence is every 2–3 years.

11) Ownership, support, and SLAs

- Document owner: People Ops (Ava Mitchell). Change requests: open a PR on the Confluence page or email people-ops@redwood.ai.
- Review cadence: annual review in January and ad-hoc updates for policy changes.
- SLA for access & IT provisioning: 5 business days standard for fully remote setups; 2 business days for expedited requests.
